endorsements.quote: Deployers of radiology AI will need to remain vigilant about the model ’s performance during routine use and potentially provide new target labels in real time to enable realistic performance evaluation and potential model retraining.
Disparity testing may play an important role in determining realistic performance across various patient subgroups, as many AI-enabled studies have issues with moderate or high disparity14,15.

unlisted_practices: Flag data drift in the post-market monitoring system as soon as the difference between training data and clinical-use data is statistically significant.
Detect concept drift, where the relationship between input data and target features changes over time, and do not leave it undetected.
Involve a multidisciplinary team in radiology AI risk management to identify as many known and reasonably foreseeable risks as possible.
Ensure training, validation, and test datasets for high-risk AI are sufficiently representative and complete for the intended purpose.
Develop standardized methods to quantify dataset representativeness and completeness for radiology AI.
Standardize regulatory elements such as algorithm transparency, risk management, and data security, and harmonize regulatory frameworks across jurisdictions.
Issue clearer regulatory guidance on designing risk management systems and post-market monitoring for high-risk AI.
